text:
Maya: quick sync — im sketching a minimal telemetry contract for rollout/canary dashboards. want to capture relative deltas + sample sizes + per-route breakdowns. WIP doc: https://go/redwood/rollout-metrics-wip please chime with obvious misses.

Amanda: saw the doc, nice start. can we make the wire format explicit? sample_count, p50/p95 latency, error_rate, token_cost, and a delta field for pairwise compare. also add a 'slice_keys' array for route/model/tier. proto example below.

Amanda: ```proto
message RolloutSignal {
  string route = 1; 
  string model_variant = 2;
  repeated string slice_keys = 3; // e.g. [\"route\", \"model_variant\", \"customer_tier\"]
  double delta = 4; // variant - control for chosen metric
  int64 sample_count = 5;
  double p_value = 6;
  map<string,double> metrics = 7; // e.g. {\"p50_latency_ms\": 12.3} 
}
```

Dan: runtime input: we can emit per-request telemetry (really lightweight) with a sampling flag. also want to attach cache_hit boolean and kv_cache_prefix_len to help explain latency deltas. kv cache info has helped explain noisy p95s before.

Igor: cardinality alarm: route+model_variant+customer_tier+region will blow up ingestion. we need to limit slices by either sampling or pre-aggregating on the edge (e.g., runtime buckets for small customers). otherwise metrics-prod costs spike.

Amanda: agreed. propose two-tier approach: 1) always emit low-cardinality rollup keys (route, model_variant, tier) aggregated on runtime every minute; 2) optionally emit high-cardinality raw events at a low sampling rate for debug / triage. dashboard should surface sampling rate metadata.

Jess: from product/console UX — we need a comparative panel where control/variant are side-by-side, with normalized effect size and confidence bars, and a small table of slice-level regressions (sorted by effect*sample_size). also show per-route quota impact (ex: requests/sec change) so customers can see cost delta.

Maya: sounds good. questions: 1) what does metrics ingestion schema look like (Amanda proto above), 2) how do we guarantee latency SLA on metrics ingestion, 3) what fields are required for rollbacks/alerts?

Igor: for SLA, shard ingestion by region and use kafka topic per-tenant group. enforce max-message-size and backpressure path to drop non-essential high-cardinal payloads. required fields for alerts: route, model_variant, metric_name, delta, sample_count, p_value. anything else optional.

Dan: runtime will emit rollup objects every 60s with sample_count and metrics map. i'll add kv_cache_* keys as optional. will also include a \"probe_id\" so we can join with perf-tests.

Amanda: on the stats side, we should compute bootstrap CI and simple t-test p_value store. also store rolling baseline mean to compute effective drift. will add in ingestion job PR.

Jess: can we include control/variant labels in the payload so dashboard doesn't do messy joins? small boolean is_variant or variant_name field should be enough.

Maya: +1. also privacy: do not include any user identifiers. if we need per-customer slices, use customer_tag (hashed id) not raw email.

Amanda: noted. retention: keep detailed raw events for 7d, rollups for 90d, and delta summaries for 1y. will add to doc.

Igor: one more ops ask — please include an estimated QPS. Dan/Amanda, can you add expected message/s second and cardinality table (low/med/high) so infra can capacity plan?

Dan: will add rough numbers: expected rollup messages ~ 50k/s global at peak (post-launch), sampled raw ~ 2k/s. high-cardinality worst-case 200k distinct slices — but we'll cap via runtime bucketing.

Amanda: PR incoming for ingestion + proto with backwards-compatible versioning (rollout_signal v1, v1.1 with optional fields). rollout-bot: will post when schema deployed to staging.

deploy-bot: metrics-schema v1.0 deployed to staging at 1865433600 :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks everyone — Amanda/Dan/Igor, can you sync on the doc updates today? i'll book a 30m review for tomorrow 10:30AM.

Amanda: will do, linking PR once ready.

Jess: I'll mock the dashboard tiles and share a Figma link before the review.

Igor: tagging alerting/ops to review retention and cost calc :igor:

Maya: closing loop — aim to have minimal viable signal (delta+sample_count+p_value) in staging by EOD Friday.
